set2.io: Discuss the selection and application of oxygen delivery
set2.q: A 70-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is on a Venturi mask set at 28%. His saturation is still below his target, and he is comfortable and alert. Which adjustment raises his fraction precisely?
opts: Add a reservoir bag to the mask

A reservoir bag converts a mask into a non-rebreather, which varies with demand and is for severe hypoxia. Adding one to a Venturi mask would not give a precise fraction. Tell: ports set a fixed fraction; a bag raises the fraction unpredictably.
confused mechanism or drug class
Switch to a nasal cannula at 2 L/min

A nasal cannula at 2 L/min delivers about 28%, which is the fraction he is already getting, and it varies with his breathing. It would not raise his fraction precisely. Tell: a cannula varies with breathing; a Venturi port is fixed.
reversed direction or value
Change to a higher-fraction port

Correct. A Venturi mask changes its fraction through different ports (24-50% when flow is adjusted from 4-10 L/min). He is stable and comfortable at 28% but below his target, so the precise adjustment is a higher-fraction port. It keeps the fraction fixed.
Switch to a non-rebreather at 15 L/min

A non-rebreather at 15 L/min would jump to 60-100% and vary with his demand. He is alert and comfortable with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, so he needs a small, precise step. Tell: the Venturi mask adjusts in small fixed steps; the non-rebreather jumps.
wrong stage or severity

set2.io: Discuss the selection and application of oxygen delivery
set2.q: A 61-year-old man with interstitial lung disease has a resting room-air saturation of 93%. When he walks the hallway it falls to 85%, and with 2 L/min by nasal cannula it rises to 92% while walking. What does he qualify for?
opts: Nothing, since rest is normal

A normal resting value does not end the evaluation, because qualification is documented at rest, with exertion and with sleep. His saturation falls to 85% when he walks and improves with oxygen, which meets the exertion criterion. Tell: always test exertion when rest is normal.
wrong stage or severity
Oxygen during sleep

The sleep criterion needs a saturation of 88% or less with a drop of 5% or more from baseline. Nothing in his stem describes sleep testing; his drop was while walking. Tell: sleep oxygen needs a nocturnal drop; his drop was with walking.
adjacent fact
Oxygen during exertion

Correct. At rest his saturation of 93% is above 88%, but walking drops it to 85%, at or below 88%, and with 2 L/min by cannula it rises to 92%. The exertion criterion is a saturation of 88% or less that improves when oxygen is given, so he qualifies for oxygen during exertion.
Oxygen at rest

Oxygen at rest requires a resting saturation of 88% or less on room air. His resting value is 93%, so he does not qualify at rest. Tell: the drop happens only while walking, so the qualification is for exertion.
ruled out by a stated finding

set2.io: Discuss the selection and application of oxygen delivery
set2.q: A 64-year-old man on postoperative day 1 after a knee replacement has an oxygen saturation of 89% on room air. He is comfortable, speaking full sentences, with no distress. Which device is the usual first choice?
opts: Simple mask at 10 L/min

A simple mask at 10 L/min is the top of its range and suits mild to moderate respiratory distress. He has no distress at all, so a mask is more than he needs as a first step. Tell: the cannula is the most commonly used device for mild hypoxia; the simple mask comes next in severity.
wrong stage or severity
Venturi mask at 50%

A Venturi mask at 50% is the top of its 24-50% range. It is a high flow device chosen when precise delivery is needed, such as in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and this man has no such need. Tell: a Venturi mask is picked for precision, not as the default for mild hypoxia.
wrong stage or severity
Nasal cannula at a low flow

Correct. After knee replacement he is comfortable and speaking full sentences with a saturation of 89% and no distress, so his hypoxia sits at the mild end. The nasal cannula, a low flow device set at 1-6 L/min, is the usual first choice for mild hypoxia and gives 24-44%.
Non-rebreather mask

A non-rebreather mask is reserved for severely hypoxic patients who are still ventilating well, and it delivers 60-100% at 10-15 L/min. He is comfortable at 89% with no distress, so this overshoots. Tell: severe hypoxia with a reservoir bag means a non-rebreather; mild hypoxia with no distress means a cannula.
wrong stage or severity

set2.io: Select the appropriate equipment and supplies necessary for initiating oxygen therapy.
set2.q: A 60-year-old man is found unresponsive and is not breathing. He has a pulse. A colleague reaches for a non-rebreather mask. Why does that device not fit his situation?
opts: Its fraction of oxygen is too low

A non-rebreather delivers a high fraction, 60-100% at 10-15 L/min, so a low fraction is not the problem. Its listed use is a severely hypoxic patient who is still ventilating well, and he is not breathing. Tell: the mask's strength is not in question; his breathing is.
ruled out by a stated finding
It is a high flow oxygen device

The non-rebreather is a low flow device, but with a high fraction; the high flow device on the list is the Venturi mask. Its flow type is not what rules it out here. Tell: he fails the mask's requirement that the patient is still ventilating well.
ruled out by a stated finding
Its bag must collapse on each breath

The dosing rule is the reverse: prevent bag collapse on inspiration, at 10-15 L/min. A bag rule does not explain why the mask fails a man who is not breathing. Tell: the non-rebreather is for patients who are still ventilating well.
ruled out by a stated finding
It is for patients ventilating well

Correct. He is unresponsive and not breathing, though he has a pulse. A non-rebreather mask is used in severely hypoxic patients who are still ventilating well, and he is not breathing at all, so the mask's listed use does not fit him.
